serp_review.query: does gmail unsubscribe remove emails already in my inbox
serp_review.observation: A standard web search returned vendor pages (macpaw, getmailbird, trimbox x5, leavemealone, an unrelated mirror). They agree that unsubscribing targets future mail; one vendor tool offers 'unsubscribe and remove existing emails' as its own feature. None cited Google's current Manage subscriptions statement that post-unsubscribe mail goes to Spam, none gave a timeline of where each email ends up, and none addressed unsubscribing before deleting so a message with the Unsubscribe control still exists, or that post-unsubscribe mail in Spam is outside an ordinary from: search.
serp_review.limitation: A single standard search, US results only; no Google help page appeared in the results; not a full SERP capture.

information_gain: A three-row 'where each email ends up' table (already received / arriving during the few-day lag / arriving after unsubscribe -> Spam with banner, per Google's current Manage subscriptions help); 'unsubscribe before deleting' ordering with its reason; the gap that post-unsubscribe mail sits in Spam outside an ordinary from: search (in:anywhere); and the Manage subscriptions sender-avatar view as a backlog starting point. The published how-to-unsubscribe-from-emails-gmail guide states in one sentence that unsubscribing does not delete messages and has a short backlog section, but does not cover Spam routing after unsubscribe, ordering, or the Spam search gap.
overlap_check: how-to-unsubscribe-from-emails-gmail (published) owns how to unsubscribe and already says unsubscribe does not delete; this draft links to it and does not repeat Manage-subscriptions finding/missing-control content. Overlap is real but the query-specific timeline and Spam-routing facts are new. Pending gmail-unsubscribe-block-delete-difference owns the action matrix, so block is limited to one FAQ. Pending gmail-unsubscribe-still-receiving-emails owns delays/multiple lists; this draft mentions the few-day lag in one table row only. delete-all-emails-from-one-sender-gmail owns sender deletion and is linked. Reviewer should judge whether the information gain is enough for a separate URL or better folded into the unsubscribe guide as a refresh.
limitations: Source and documentation review only; no live Gmail mailbox test was run and no screenshots were produced.
